entities.name: Ailill Molt
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ailill Molt, son of Nath Í, was a pivotal figure in the post-Roman Iron Age of Ireland, reigning as High King of Ireland from approximately 463 CE until his death in 482 CE. His tenure marks a critical juncture in the early historical period, bridging the mythological sagas of the Uí Néill dynasty's rise with the emerging historical record. As the last High King not belonging to the dominant Uí Néill lineage for centuries, Ailill Molt's reign represents a final assertion of independence by the Connachta, the tribal grouping from which he sprang, before the Uí Néill consolidated their hegemonic control over much of the island.

During his approximate two-decade rule, Ailill Molt navigated a complex political landscape characterized by inter-dynastic rivalries and the gradual Christianization of Ireland. Traditional accounts place his power base in Connacht, though his authority as High King extended across various petty kingdoms, likely enforced through military prowess and strategic alliances. His accession followed the death of his father, Nath Í, also a High King, indicating a dynastic claim to the supreme kingship that temporarily defied the Uí Néill ascendancy established by figures like Niall of the Nine Hostages. His cognomen, "Molt" (meaning "ram"), while of uncertain origin, hints at a formidable or perhaps stubborn character, fitting for a ruler who resisted the tide of Uí Néill dominance.
